newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS--API stock drops seen keeping oil prices hot.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS--API stock drops seen keeping oil prices hot.

text.p: Draws in crude oil and distillate stocks in Wednesday's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) helped boost NYMEX futures prices during afterhours Access trade.

"Crude stocks appeared to be correcting on what happened in last week's report," said Peter Keavey, trader with ING Derivatives Clearing, Inc, referring to the surprise 9.3-million-barrel build a week ago. API said crude stocks fell by 6.61 million barrels last week, though five million barrels of that decline was on the West Coast.
"This report's not too exciting. The market's in an uptrend and this shouldn't do much to change it," Keavey said.

The API also reported a draw in distillate stocks of 827,000 barrels for the week, including a draw in PADD 1 heating oil stocks of 23,000 barrels. Gasoline stocks were put 2.89 million barrels lower, while refinery runs fell 3.2 percentage points to 90.7 percent of capacity.

"A lot of people thought last week's numbers were erroneous. This report seemed to correct all that. If you put the two together, things make more sense," said Thomas Blakeslee, a trader with Cargill Investor Services.
Other market players focused on refined product stocks, which continued to hover at very low levels.

"We're one week closer to winter and distillate stocks fell," said Tom Knight, a trader with Fina Inc, noting heating oil stocks fell in the huge East Coast market as well. "I believe we're setting up for another rally in distillates."
"The runs falling was the biggest feature. We're seeing the effects of refinery problems, and that has been the driving force of the market," said Knight.
"We're seeing a lot more refinery maintenance in these numbers," Blakeslee agreed.
Low refinery output was keeping pressure on product stocks, which in turn was having a dramatic effect in Gulf Coast gasoline markets.

"It's all going to be a function of when are we going to see some barrels on offer," Knight said, referring to spot gasoline markets in Houston where prices have soared amid widespread buying by refiners and, more recently, speculators.

Gulf traders said the 2.9-million-barrel draw on total U.S. gasoline stocks could only strengthen differentials on "M4"-grade conventional unleaded, which had firmed two cents a gallon Wednesday even before release of the API weekly data.
"Gasoline stocks are near their historical lows," he said, estimating "outstanding" implied demand of about 8.1 million barrels per day.
